Kinetic sand is a great way to provide sensory input while still working on a multitude of skills.  I love to use cookie cutters in the sand to work on bilateral skills, pressure and and force regulation.  Cutting with sand is a great introduction to snipping and provides additional sensory feedback. Kids who are struggling with writing tend to be more willing to practice writing on different surfaces. Try sand and use a paint brush for smooth lines.  #occupationaltherapy #ot #sensoryactivities #finemotorskills #sensory #schoolbasedot

Kinetic Art Explained: Art History & The Science of Movement  | Seed Gallery Kinetic Art is a dynamic genre in Art History defined by works that contain movement perceivable by the viewer or employ motion to achieve their intent. Deriving from the Greek word kinesis, this term applies to any medium, from painting to sculpture, where movement is an integral part of the aesthetic. We explore how Kinetic Art challenges the traditional stasis of the art object. We trace its evolution from canvas paintings that create multidimensional movement to modern solar-powered installations and sculptures that use wind and water. By making motion the primary focus, Kinetic Art invites a deeper interaction between the work and the observer. At Seed Gallery, the Art History and Economics Glossary explores the principles of visual structure and theory that shape artistic expression across time. 👉 Subscribe for ongoing insights into art history, materials, and visual culture.
